newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dah Hwa buys a China petrochemical firm.
newsitem.headline: Dah Hwa buys a China petrochemical firm.

text.p: Leather trader and distributor Dah Hwa International (Holdings) Ltd said on Sunday it had agreed to buy a 49 percent stake in Shenzhen Petrochemical Chemical Fibres Co Ltd for HK$35.72 million from Good Nation Investment Ltd.

Shenzhen Petrochemical Chemical Fibres, a joint venture firm in China, is 51 percent owned by Shenzhen Petrochemical (Holdings) Co Ltd and 49 percent owned by Good Nation, Dah Hwa said in a statement.
The joint venture, established in 1991, is one of China's largest manufacturers of polypropylene chemical fibres, which is used in manufacturing nylon materials for sports and travel bags, it said.

Dah Hwa said Good Nation would be given approximately 4.13 percent of its existing share capital and 3.96 percent of the enlarged share capital, totalling 21.94 million shares, as payment for the acquisition. The 21.94 million shares equalled HK$1.809 a share.
The company added Good Nation had promised it would not sell or transfer the shares within two years from the date of completion of the deal.
